fatal_errors: The proposed machine-learning intervention replaces the target physical method of high-energy ball milling followed by spark plasma sintering.
The initial CoCrFeNiTi elemental-powder system and all critical milling and sintering conditions are absent.
The cited evidence concerns phase prediction and stacking-fault-energy modeling, not demonstrated microstructure refinement, densification, or mechanical-property optimization by the proposed method.
No quantitative phase fractions, grain size, density, hardness, yield stress, or compressive strength are predicted.
explanation: The hypothesis is only broadly aligned with high-entropy-alloy phase and property optimization. It does not reconstruct the target method, which uses high-energy ball milling to generate lattice strain and nanocrystalline material, followed by rapid SPS densification that preserves an 83% FCC/17% BCC structure. Its generic references to entropy, lattice distortion, and atomic-size difference have limited conceptual overlap but omit Hall–Petch strengthening, accumulated dislocations, solid-solution strengthening, titanium-dependent phase stabilization, and porosity suppression. The baseline and boundaries address computational alloy design rather than cast-alloy defects or the milling–sintering process window. The proposed comparison could test whether ML-guided design helps generally, but it lacks fixed composition, processing controls, quantitative endpoints, and phase/grain-size measurements needed to discriminate the target mechanism. The evidence supports phase-prediction approaches only and does not validate the full claim of refinement and property improvement.
